text:
Kev: ran an nsys trace on the regression where latency jumps at batch sizes >=4. KV prefetch and kernel selection overlap in the timeline and it's impossible to tell which is causing the conservative kernel choice. link: https://perf.internal/runs/2070005555 :eyes:
Olivia: can you paste the exact nsys command and a tiny timeline snippet? makes it easier to repro locally
Kev: command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run-2070005555.nsys \n  ./bin/redwood-runtime --workload=batch=8 seq=2048 model=starling
```
perfetto snapshot: long CUDA kernel blocks interleaved with short host NVTX-prefetch ranges (green). The 'kernel_select' spans are lumped into the host time and overlapping with prefetch.
Aj: my guess is our current NVTX markings are too coarse. We basically do one big "req" range and then generic "kernel" labels. We need granular per-request per-step ranges so perf tools can filter by req id.
Maria: agreed. Proposed naming: `req/<reqid>/<step>` where step ∈ {enqueue,kv_prefetch,kernel_select,launch,postprocess}. Example: `req/0x7f3a2/kv_prefetch`. Pros: prefix filters are trivial in perf tools. Cons: string length and NVTX cost.
Kev: alternative: use short ids in nvtx and emit a separate mapping event in logs or a small metadata NVTX range at request start that maps id -> verbose metadata. eg: `r7fa2` in timeline + separate log line with full context. Keeps traces compact.
DevTraceBot: note: some drivers cap NVTX label length (256). stay under that.
Olivia: also we should push kernel selection details into NVTX right before calling the kernel: `ks:matmul.q8_0|b=8|s=2048`. That way the kernel block carries selector metadata.
Aj: push/pop overhead? NVTX push/pop is fast but if we add it for every tiny micro-kernel it could add noise. any numbers?
Kev: did a small microbenchmark: 10k push/pop pairs on a pinned thread added ~1.8ms total. For a normal request with ~120 kernel launches that's ~0.015ms per request — negligible for large seq. But at tiny batch sizes it becomes measurable. we'll gate behind `PERF_NVTX=1` env var.
Maria: sample NVTX helper (pseudo):
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_FMT("req/%s/kv_prefetch", req_hex);
// prefetch...
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_FMT("req/%s/ks:%s|b=%d", req_hex, kname, batch);
launch_kernel();
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
Kev: also add a host-span around scheduling windows: `sched_window/<worker>` to capture enqueue->launch delays. That was visible in my trace as a thin yellow band that matched spikes in kernel_select_ms.
perf-bot: correlation found: when kv_prefetch overlaps kernel_select, kernel_select median increased from 0.4ms -> 2.2ms and we more frequently pick fallback kernels. suspect shared L2 / PCIe contention and extra memcpy path.
Olivia: next steps I propose:
1) implement per-request per-step NVTX ranges behind `PERF_NVTX` flag (short hex ids by default)
2) annotate kernel selector with chosen kernel string and small params (batch, seq)
3) run controlled nsys+perfetto sweep on isolated node with cpu isolation and `PERF_NVTX=1` for batch sizes [1,2,4,8] and seqs [512,1024,2048]
4) collect traces and surface with perf links + a short writeup
Aj: I'll open a PR with helper macros and the short-id mapping. I'll also add a switch to use long names when `PERF_NVTX_VERBOSE=1`.
Kev: will run the sweep tomorrow AM and attach the run ids. tagging @Maria for dashboarding: we should emit a metric `nvtx_overhead_ms` and `kernel_select_ms` by model+batch so we can watch rollout.
Maria: ack. I'll add a dashboard and a small doc in the infra perf playbook describing the nvtx naming conventions and the gating flags. Also will make sure the logs contain the mapping table (short id -> full details) so we can search via Kibana.
Olivia: thanks — scheduling a 30m trace review tomorrow 10:30. please upload nsys and perfetto files to the perf bucket and paste links here. :thumbsup:
Kev: uploaded run: https://perf.internal/runs/2070005555 and small perfetto snapshot: https://perf.internal/snap/2070005555.pftrace
Aj: PR incoming. I'll include a small microbench in the PR that measures nvtx push/pop cost under our runtime thread pool.
DevTraceBot: reminder: NVTX push/pop pairs are thread-scoped. ensure we don't push on worker and pop on different thread — that'll assert in some analyzers.
Maria: final note: watch out for sampling artifacts when we annotate lots of short ranges — perfetto/nsys can coalesce tiny ranges into single visual block. We'll add both coarse and fine ranges so higher-level windows are still readable.
Olivia: great discussion. see you in the review tomorrow.
